question.text: 'Saksham Skills Pvt Ltd' is a For Profit Enterprise (FPE) seeking registration on BSE-SSE. For SIA assessment of primacy of social intent under SEBI ICDR Regulations, what minimum threshold of eligible activities directed at the target population must be demonstrated?

answer.text: At least 50% of the immediately preceding 3-year average of revenues, expenditure or beneficiaries
At least 85% of the immediately preceding 3-year average of revenues, expenditure or beneficiaries
At least 75% of the immediately preceding 3-year average of revenues, expenditure or beneficiaries
At least 67% of the immediately preceding 3-year average of revenues, expenditure or beneficiaries

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI ICDR Regulations require an FPE to demonstrate at least 67% of its immediately preceding 3-year average of either revenues, expenditure, or beneficiary count directed toward eligible activities to the target population. Any one of the three tests satisfies the threshold. The Trap: Option A (50%) is a simple majority — incorrect. Option C (75%) confuses with some CSR spending norms. Option B (85%) is the Section 11 income-application threshold under the Income Tax Act for NPOs, not the FPE eligibility threshold. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 3 (SSE Registration), Ch 10 (Taxation — 85% application under Section 11), and III-A (Compliance). SIAs must NOT confuse the 67% FPE primacy test with the 85% application-of-income test. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Ask the SE for 3-year audited financials and beneficiary MIS separately. Compute all three ratios (revenue/expenditure/beneficiary) — the SE may pass only one, which is sufficient. Document which test passed in your working papers so subsequent reviewers can retrace.
